spec: Russell 3000 members as held by the iShares Russell 3000 ETF (IWV), from its quarterly SEC N-PORT filings: the latest snapshot whose period ends on or before each formation date, used from its period date, about two months before the filing was public (IWV's holdings stand in for the index membership FTSE Russell had already published). Holdings mapped to tickers with OpenFIGI and checked against N-PORT's own value per share. Daily prices 2020–2025: price history for 82.2% of the requested symbols; 14.2% no longer served by the vendor (HTTP 404) and 3.6% failed the fetch or the data checks; the fetch-coverage rule, which counts 404s and failed data checks as resolved, is met at 98.8%. Screens on the window's length (at least 300 bars), mean point-in-time price (at least $5, anchored to N-PORT) and mean dollar volume (at least $10M a day), volatility and missing data; the 500 most liquid enter the pair search.

Pairs within one Fama–French 49 industry (SEC SIC codes); positive return correlation ≥ 0.25; two-direction Engle–Granger p < 0.05 (Bonferroni across directions); half-life 4–25 days on the cointegrating spread; quality score > 0.4. The whole selection re-run every 126 trading days on the trailing three years; open positions run off.
Two-state Kalman filter (slope and intercept) on log prices centred on their burn-in means, so β is a hedge ratio and signals are invariant to vendor back-adjustment.

One β-locked z-score against its mean and standard deviation over the last 30–60 bars, frozen at the signal. Entry |z| ≥ 1.8; target once z reverts past −0.5 (long) or +0.5 (short); stop 1.5 further against; time stop max(10, min(⌊2.5 × half-life⌋, 25)) days. Gates: pair quality ≥ 0.55, 20-day correlation ≥ 0.20, β in [0.25, 4], at least 50 bars of pair history, locked-spread standard deviation at most 0.30, the smaller leg's 20-day dollar ADV at least $1M, an ex-ante round-trip cost (with borrow over the maximum hold) below 1% of equity, a 30-day pause after three consecutive losing trades on a pair; no new signal on a day the book lost more than 3%. No regime gate.

$100M notional; 3–10% of equity per pair before risk scaling (2.2% to 10.0% as traded), scaled by the win rate of the last five closed trades and the volatility of recent daily returns; 30% gross cap on exposure at entry; at most 8 entries a day, ordered by signal strength × pair quality; no shared legs; daily mark-to-market; a kill switch that flattens the book at a 15% drawdown from peak, a 5% daily loss or gross exposure at entry above 30%.

Per execution: $0.002 a share (minimum $0.50), half the quoted spread by 20-day dollar ADV, square-root impact (Y = 0.3, cap 50 bp); one 0.38% a year borrow fee on the short notional, charged over the days held.
The same rule on the same formations from 14 February 2023, one continuous simulation cut into 63-day test windows; there is no model to refit.

Probabilistic and deflated Sharpe, Newey–West t, Politis–White block bootstrap, power and upper bounds under a non-normal AR(1) variance, a Bonferroni Sharpe hurdle for 32 trials and two field-wide hurdles, Ledoit–Wolf Sharpe-difference test; eight-factor attribution; the anatomy of the result (shortfall, exit race, decay, persistence, half-lives, capacity, cash); Gatev distance method and random pairs under the same costs and t + 1 fills. A declared family of 38 variants with Hansen's SPA, White's Reality Check, the Romano–Wolf stepdown, the model confidence set, PBO and a deflated Sharpe ratio at its effective number of trials; robustness checks over start dates, regimes, the candidate pairs' persistence and clustered standard errors.
